note: The only parameters of the arm guides: the match spelling (M2, M3) and the quantifier names (Q2). Each 'from' occurs exactly once in the template and 'to' keeps its line count; scripts/trial-guides.ts rejects any other difference.

M2.from:
- `match (payer) { CUSTOMER => …, COMPANY { name } => … }` has one case per variant, each once, and gives a value of
  one type; a case names the fields of its variant it reads.
M2.to:
- `match (payer) { when { kind: Payer.CUSTOMER }: …; when { kind: Payer.COMPANY, name }: …; }` has one case per variant, each once, and gives a value of
  one type; a case names its variant by the tag (`kind: Payer.COMPANY`, the union's discriminator) and then the fields of its variant it reads, and ends with `;`.

M3.from:
- `match (payer) { CUSTOMER => …, COMPANY { name } => … }` has one case per variant, each once, and gives a value of
  one type; a case names the fields of its variant it reads.
M3.to:
- `match(payer).with({ kind: Payer.CUSTOMER }, p => …).with({ kind: Payer.COMPANY }, p => … p.name …).exhaustive()` has one `.with` per variant, each once, ends with `.exhaustive()`, and gives a value of
  one type; a `.with` names its variant by the tag (`kind: Payer.COMPANY`, the union's discriminator), and its handler's parameter is the matched variant, whose fields it reads as `p.name`.

Q2.from: A subset is written with `every`: `required.every(s => confirmed.includes(s))`.
Q2.to: A subset is written with `forall`: `required.forall(s => confirmed.includes(s))`.
